                 MOTION TO INTERVENE AND PROTEST OF THE
         ALASKA COMMERCIAL FISHERIES CONSERVATION ALLIANCE

Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's Rules of Practice
and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.214, the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation
Alliance (ACFCA) hereby submits this Motion to Intervene and Protest in the above-
captioned proceeding regarding the application for a preliminary permit filed by
DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV, LLC (DeepGreen or Applicant) on February 11, 2026, as
supplemented on June 26, 2026, pursuant to Section 4(f) of the Federal Power Act (FPA),
16 U.S.C. § 797(f). This motion is filed in response to the Notice of Preliminary Permit
Application Accepted for Filing and Soliciting Comments, Motions to Intervene, and
Competing Applications published in the Federal Register on September 4, 2026, 91 FR
56879, Docket No. P-15423-000. This filing is timely under the November 2, 2026
intervention deadline established in that notice.


I. COMMUNICATIONS AND SERVICE


All communications, service of pleadings, and technical discovery documents relating to
this proceeding should be addressed to:


Russell Clark, President and Authorized Representative
Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance
EIN: 42-5019410
117 Deepwood Court, Kenai, Alaska 99611
Telephone: 918-953-0039
Electronic Mail: acfca@acfcaadvocacy.org
 ACFCA        requests     that      FERC        Contact       Christopher Brosman
(Christopher.Brosman@ferc.gov | 202-502-8573) add ACFCA to the service list for all
filings in Docket No. P-15423-000. ACFCA will file electronically through the
Commission's eFiling system at ferconline.ferc.gov/eFiling.aspx.


II. INTEREST OF THE INTERVENOR


The Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance is a nonprofit corporation
incorporated under Alaska law on September 10, 2026, with EIN 42-5019410, organized
as a business league under IRC Section 501(c)(6) to represent the common commercial
fishing business interests of Alaska commercial fishing permit holders, including holders
of Upper Cook Inlet drift gillnet (S03H) and set gillnet (S04H) limited entry permits issued
by the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Entry Commission.
ACFCA members depend directly on the ecological health, biological productivity, and
migratory integrity of wild salmon stocks in Upper Cook Inlet for their livelihoods. The
proposed DeepGreen Cook Inlet Subsea-Compute and Infrastructure Hub Project
encompasses a project footprint of approximately 1,650 acres of Cook Inlet seabed in the
Upper Cook Inlet East Foreland Corridor, located west of Nikiski in the Kenai Peninsula
Borough, in waters utilized by ACFCA's commercial fishing membership. The project
proposes to install: (1) approximately 330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines; (2) 66
modular subsea-compute hives functioning as data center pods powered by the turbine
array and passively cooled by ambient seawater circulation; (3) an approximately 3.5-mile
long, 115-kilovolt hybrid power and fiber-optic armored subsea cable; and (4) a cable
landing site positioned within the Nikiski Industrial Corridor between the Agrium Kenai
Nitrogen Operations facility and the Kenai Liquefied Natural Gas Plant. The estimated
annual generation is 100 megawatts, utilized primarily to power the subsea data center
infrastructure.
The installation of 330 to 350 marine turbines and 66 subsea data center pods across a
1,650-acre footprint in active commercial fishing grounds, in water ranging from 45 to 166
feet in depth, represents a direct, substantial, and immediate threat to commercial fishing
gear, vessel navigation, salmon migration corridors, and the marine environment upon
which ACFCA's membership depends. ACFCA has a distinct organizational interest in
this proceeding that cannot be adequately represented by any existing party.
This motion is filed under the emergency regulatory action authority granted to ACFCA's
President by Bylaws Section 7.4, which authorizes the President to file FERC
interventions without prior Board approval when the intervention deadline requires
immediate action. The Board of Directors will ratify this filing at its next scheduled meeting.


III. STATEMENT OF PROTEST AND TECHNICAL DEFICIENCIES


ACFCA protests the DeepGreen preliminary permit application on the grounds that, as
FERC itself has identified through deficiency correspondence, and as described below,
 the application omits critical thermodynamic, hydrodynamic, structural, and fisheries
impact data necessary for the Commission to evaluate environmental and operational
risks to Upper Cook Inlet commercial fishing operations and marine resources.


A. Thermal Load and Subsea Heat Dissipation.
The proposed 100-megawatt subsea data center and associated power infrastructure will
generate a continuous thermal load that must be dissipated into Upper Cook Inlet
seawater through passive cooling of the 66 subsea-compute hive pods. This continuous
heat output, derived from both the conversion losses of the marine hydrokinetic turbines
and the computing load of the data center pods, is the equivalent of approximately 341.2
million BTUs per hour. Maintaining even a 1°C localized temperature rise in the
surrounding water column requires continuous water exchange at a rate of approximately
380,000 to 387,000 gallons per minute, calculated using the specific heat capacity of
Upper Cook Inlet seawater at prevailing temperature and salinity conditions. The
application provides no thermal plume model, no dispersion analysis, and no heat budget
for the project area under any operational scenario. Without this analysis, the Commission
cannot evaluate the project's effect on salmon water temperature preference thresholds,
migration timing, or habitat utilization in the East Foreland Corridor.


B. Failure to Address Tidal Variation, Passive Cooling Collapse, and the
Compounded Power-Cooling Failure.
The proposed project's passive seawater cooling system relies entirely on natural tidal
circulation to dissipate heat from the 66 subsea-compute hive pods. Upper Cook Inlet is
characterized by mixed semi-diurnal tides with high diurnal inequality, producing up to
four zero-velocity slack tide periods per day and reduced flow during neap tide cycles.
During slack tide, the passive cooling mechanism collapses completely and the 100-
megawatt continuous thermal load accumulates in the project area as a superheated
thermal mass.
The application fails to address a compounded failure state that is inherent to the project
design: the marine hydrokinetic turbines cease generating electricity during the same
zero-velocity slack tide periods that eliminate passive cooling. ACFCA identifies this as a
double failure condition: maximum thermal accumulation from continuous computing load
occurring simultaneously with zero turbine power output. Any active cooling response
during slack tide, such as electric pumps to force water circulation through the pod array,
requires power drawn from battery storage or a grid interconnection that the application
does not describe. The application contains no computational fluid dynamics modeling of
heat accumulation during the combined power-cooling failure state, no thermal threshold
analysis for salmon species present in the project area, and no assessment of the
frequency and duration of these compounded failure periods.
Each available engineering solution to the passive cooling problem constitutes a
materially different project than what was filed in February 2026 and supplemented June
26, 2026. Active cooling pumps require power infrastructure not described in the
application. Thermal energy buffers sufficient to absorb 100 megawatts of heat through a
 two-hour slack tide at depths of 45 to 166 feet would materially expand the project
footprint. Variable computing load management: throttling capacity according to Cook
Inlet tidal schedules: fundamentally undermines the commercial premise of a data center.
Any of these solutions requires a substantially revised application with new environmental
analysis. FERC cannot evaluate the feasibility or approvability of this project until
DeepGreen describes its proposed solution to the power-cooling compound failure, the
infrastructure required, and the resulting effect on net power output and environmental
footprint.


C. Structural Deficiency Identified by FERC.
FERC has already identified structural data deficiencies in the application. The application
describes the project using generalized language about the turbine array and
infrastructure without providing specific counts, power ratings, physical dimensions,
anchoring systems, or sediment protection plans for individual turbine and data center
pod units. As FERC's deficiency correspondence has noted, the application does not
provide the specific number of proposed generators along with power ratings for each
turbine and generator unit. Without this data, the Commission cannot evaluate turbine
fish-strike risks, gear entanglement hazards for commercial fishing vessels, silt
disturbance during installation and operation, organism entrainment in turbine intakes, or
navigation safety in the 1,650-acre project footprint.


D. Omission of Commercial Fishing Impact Assessment.
The application contains no assessment of impact on existing commercial fishing
operations in the project area. Upper Cook Inlet supports over 1,300 active limited entry
commercial fishing permits for drift gillnet, set gillnet, and other gear types, contributing to
a fishery with historical annual revenues of approximately $9.5 to $10 million. The federal
government has issued commercial fishery disaster declarations for Cook Inlet
commercial salmon for the years 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023. The proposed 1,650-
acre project footprint overlaps directly with established commercial fishing grounds in the
East Foreland Corridor. The cable landing site located between the Agrium Kenai
Nitrogen Operations and the Kenai LNG Plant in the Nikiski Industrial Corridor adds a
second zone of gear conflict. Section 4(e) of the Federal Power Act, 16 U.S.C. § 797(e),
requires the Commission to consider the protection and utilization of established resource
uses, including commercial fishing, in evaluating any license-related action. A preliminary
permit proceeding that advances a project of this scale without any commercial fishing
impact assessment fails that obligation.


E. Misrepresentation of Relationship with Alaska Energy Authority.
ACFCA has reason to believe that the DeepGreen preliminary permit application
misrepresented the applicant's relationship with the Alaska Energy Authority (AEA). A
material misrepresentation to a federal agency in a FERC filing constitutes a violation of
18 U.S.C. § 1001. ACFCA requests that the Commission investigate and confirm the
actual nature of any claimed relationship between DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV, LLC and
 AEA, and consider suspension of the preliminary permit review pending resolution of any
misrepresentation findings.


IV. ADDITIONAL GROUNDS


A. Applicant's Lack of Energy Development Experience.
DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV, LLC was incorporated in Delaware in January 2026, one
month before filing its FERC preliminary permit application in February 2026. The
applicant's parent company, DeepGreen Holdings LLC, is managed by Louis Wolfson of
Needham, Massachusetts, whose professional background is in luxury real estate
development. The Commission should consider whether the applicant has the technical
competence and financial resources to conduct the environmental and engineering
studies a preliminary permit authorizes, and should require evidence of technical
qualifications as a condition of any permit issuance.


B. Proximity to Existing Industrial Corridor.
The proposed cable landing site in the Nikiski Industrial Corridor, sited between the
Agrium Kenai Nitrogen Operations facility and the Kenai LNG Plant, introduces a second
zone of commercial fishing gear conflict along the established Kenai Spur Highway
industrial waterfront. ACFCA's members fish waters adjacent to this corridor. The
cumulative impact of the turbine array and the cable landing zone on commercial fishing
access has not been assessed.


V. REQUESTED RELIEF


ACFCA respectfully requests that the Commission:


1. Grant ACFCA's Motion to Intervene and designate ACFCA as a formal party to Docket
No. P-15423-000 with full rights to participate in all proceedings, submit comments and
protests, engage in discovery, and appeal Commission orders.
2. Require DeepGreen to supplement its preliminary permit application with: (a) a
complete thermal load and plume model for the 66 subsea-compute pods under all tidal
flow conditions including slack tide; (b) specific turbine counts, power ratings, and
physical dimensions for all marine hydrokinetic turbines and data center pod units within
the 1,650-acre project footprint; (c) a commercial fishing impact assessment covering all
gear types, permit holders, vessel transit routes, and fishing seasons affected by both the
turbine array and the cable landing zone; and (d) a full hydrodynamic model of project
effects on salmon migration in the East Foreland Corridor.
 3. Investigate and confirm the actual relationship between DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV,
LLC and the Alaska Energy Authority, and suspend further action on the preliminary
permit application pending resolution of any material misrepresentation findings.
4. Require evidence of DeepGreen's technical and financial qualifications to conduct the
engineering and environmental studies authorized by a preliminary permit before
proceeding further.
5. Add ACFCA to the service list for all correspondence, orders, and filings in Docket No.
P-15423-000.


VI. CONCLUSION


The Upper Cook Inlet commercial fishing fleet has operated in the East Foreland Corridor
for generations and represents a federally recognized fishery that has sustained Alaska
coastal communities through five consecutive years of federal disaster declarations. The
DeepGreen preliminary permit application, as filed, lacks the technical and environmental
analysis necessary for the Commission to evaluate its compatibility with existing resource
uses in Upper Cook Inlet. ACFCA urges the Commission to grant intervention, require the
supplemental data identified above, and investigate the AEA relationship before any
further administrative action.


Respectfully submitted,
